journey.title: Acquire capacity and watch what it costs
journey.purpose: The primary loop. An operator finds they need a machine, sees the cost and the minimum billable unit before committing, watches the instance become a trusted node, and then lets it drain or destroys it deliberately. The journey exists to make cost and expiry visible at every step, because both are irreversible once missed.

steps.intent: See the whole current liability and notice there is not enough capacity for the work at hand.
Choose a size, region and lifetime, and read the estimated cost and the minimum billable unit before committing. Hourly rounding is stated here rather than discovered on an invoice.
Understand that credit is reserved before any provider is called, so a refusal costs nothing and leaves nothing behind.
Watch the instance move from creating to running, with elapsed cost beginning to accrue from the running transition.
See that enrollment is queued rather than failed, and that the instance is still real, metered and expiring while bridge catches up.
See the new instance alongside the rest of the fleet with its remaining lifetime visible.
Destroy the instance by typing its name, and read the settled figure rather than a live estimate.
